scenes.title: Night 1 unfamiliar bedroom sleep suite: right hemisphere sleeps while left hemisphere taps awake at deviant tones
scenes.era: 2016 Brown University Sleep & Vision Laboratory two-night neuroimaging study

layout.description: Bright architectural sleep-laboratory bedroom with crisp white hotel-style platform bed at center, walnut bedside stand holding an unmarked finger-tap button pad on the right, and an observation window on the left.

positions.who: Volunteer sleeper (clothed matte-white porcelain figure with smooth featureless solid matte-white egg-shaped oval head in slate-blue cotton pajama cardigan and soft white sleep earphones)
positions.where: lying supine on the crisp white hotel-style mattress with right porcelain hand resting beside the bedside response pad
positions.facing: upward and angled slightly toward the bedside response pad

positions.who: Sleep neuroscientist (clothed matte-white porcelain figure with smooth featureless solid matte-white egg-shaped oval head in crisp white lab coat over charcoal knit)
positions.where: standing beside the bed checking scalp sensor leads, then watching through the observation window
positions.facing: facing the bed and dual-hemisphere waveform monitor

props.name: crisp white hotel-style pillow, soft acoustic earphones, and slender scalp sensor leads
props.period_detail: unmarked white cotton bedding paired with minimal white clinical sleep leads
props.physical_behavior: sleeper shifts restlessly on the unfamiliar pillow on Night 1 and snaps awake when an oddball earphone tone arrives

props.name: unmarked bedside finger-tap response pad and dual waveform display
props.period_detail: clean brushed-aluminum button pad beside a text-free dual wave monitor
props.physical_behavior: right index finger briskly depresses the button pad as the top left-hemisphere wave trace spikes

actions.verb_sequence: lies still on the crisp white pillow wearing slender sensor leads -> briskly presses the bedside button pad with right index finger the instant an irregular tone sounds

reactions.reaction: leans closer to the unmarked dual-wave display comparing the shallow top trace against the deep slow bottom trace

scenes.wardrobe: Volunteer in slate-blue buttoned cotton pajama cardigan and trousers; researcher in crisp white lab coat over charcoal sweater.
scenes.lighting: Clean high-key cool architectural daylight-moonlight balance with soft rim illumination.
scenes.recognition_hook: On Night 1 in an unfamiliar bed, half your brain stays on dolphin-like night-watch duty and snaps your hand awake three times faster.

key_visual.description: porcelain sleeper in slate-blue pajama cardigan lying on a crisp white hotel-style bed wearing slender scalp leads and pressing a bedside button pad while a researcher watches behind glass

scenes.title: Night 2 adaptation & familiar pillowcase cue calming left-hemisphere sentinel
scenes.era: 2016 Brown University Night 2 session & everyday hotel bedroom

layout.description: Same minimalist hotel-style bedroom with sleeper slipping a familiar oatmeal-linen home pillowcase onto the hotel pillow before resting deeply.

positions.who: Traveler sleeper (porcelain figure in slate-blue pajama cardigan)
positions.where: seated at the edge of the bed smoothing a familiar home pillowcase over the pillow

props.name: folded oatmeal-linen home pillowcase over hotel pillow
props.period_detail: unmarked natural woven linen pillow slip carried in an open overnight bag
props.physical_behavior: porcelain hands smooth the familiar linen pillowcase flat before shoulders sink into deep stillness

actions.verb_sequence: slips a folded oatmeal-linen pillowcase over the hotel pillow -> settles head deeply onto the linen with relaxed motionless hands

reactions.reaction: chest rises in slow even breaths without twitching toward the bedside pad

scenes.lighting: Warm calm architectural evening studio balance.
scenes.recognition_hook: By Night 2 — or when familiar scent/bedding cues disarm novelty — both hemispheres drop into matching deep delta waves.

scenes.title: Contained Living 4-Color 3D Brain dorsal split: sleeping right hemisphere vs vigilant left default-mode network

layout.description: Bright white architectural gallery housing a Contained Living 4-Color 3D Brain dorsal cutaway on a matte-white pedestal.

props.name: translucent dorsal 3D brain cutaway
props.period_detail: contained subsurface four-color internal glow with zero external particle spill
props.physical_behavior: right hemisphere pulses with deep pearl-aqua slow waves while left default-mode hubs glow warm amber-gold and crimson-red

actions.verb_sequence: pulses calm pearl-aqua waves across the right hemisphere -> flashes amber-gold and crimson-red sentinel signals along the left prefrontal-thalamic loop

reactions.reaction: by Night 2 both hemispheres synchronize into matching deep electric cyan-blue and pearl-aqua slow waves

scenes.recognition_hook: Visualizes half-asleep asymmetric human brain activity side-by-side inside one skull.
